text: Last class you said: do I have to take off my shoes? You don't have to pay.
Today it is lunch time, and the food in Istanbul smells wonderful.
What does it taste like? It tastes a little sour.
Here we are, Marlene. There is no menu. You look at the food and you point.
Everything looks delicious! What are those green things?
They are peppers stuffed with rice. They taste a little sour with lemon.
I would like to try them. Can I have a half portion?
Sure. And I recommend the grilled chicken. It smells wonderful, right?
Yes, it does. And what is that white drink? What does it taste like?
That is ayran, a yogurt drink. It tastes salty, not sweet. Try it!
Mmm, it tastes strange but good! And Turkish coffee after lunch?
Yes, but it is a little bitter. Have a piece of baklava with it.
Can I have a half portion, please?

Welcome to our lokanta. This is how it works. You do not need a menu. Come to the front and look at the food behind the glass. You point at the dishes you want, and we bring them to your table. Today we have lentil soup. It tastes a little sour, because we serve it with lemon. We also have stuffed peppers with rice, and grilled chicken with salad. A half portion is cheaper, and it is a good size for lunch. To drink, try ayran. It is a cold yogurt drink, and it tastes salty. Please pay at the front when you finish. Enjoy your meal.

Hello, everybody, and welcome to my cooking class in Istanbul. I am Selin. Today we make two famous Turkish sweets. The first is baklava. It has thin pastry, butter, sugar and pistachio nuts, so it tastes very sweet. If you are allergic to nuts, please tell me now. The second is Turkish delight. It looks like small colorful cubes, and it smells of roses. At the end, we drink Turkish coffee together. It tastes strong and a little bitter, so many people drink it with a sweet. The class takes two hours, and you can take the sweets home in a box.

First, you walk into a small lokanta near the Grand Bazaar. Then you look at the dishes behind the glass, and the food looks delicious. Next, you point at the stuffed peppers and you ask for a half portion. After that, you try ayran, and it tastes salty. Finally, you finish with a small glass of tea and you pay at the front.
The peppers are stuffed with rice.
Turkish coffee is a little bitter.
A half portion is enough for lunch.
Can I have a half portion, please?
